headSubject: fix(runtimehost): REG-243 -- /model-reload names that it does not refresh UI metadata catalogs
summary: Executed Phases 1-3 of PLAN_CLOSE_ALL_OPEN_2026-09-22.md end to end: closed REG-240 (identityTables cache bug), REG-241 (orchestration subscribers never re-registered on reload), REG-242 (DocumentRenderController pinned to boot model + new structural checker scripts/quality/check-model-provider-injection.py wired into aiKnowledge [49/49]), and REG-243 (/model-reload response now names that it does not refresh UI metadata catalogs, per an explicit owner decision on the plan's deferred Phase 3 branch: document the limit rather than couple /model-reload to the build-time classifier). Every item closed with a genuine RED-proof (stub the fix, confirm exactly the predicted tests fail, restore, grep-confirm clean) and a guard block, not just a green run. Also fixed a real scripts/ coverage-ratchet regression the new checker caused by adding it without a --calibrate self-test -- added one (7 controls), then honestly re-pinned the floor citing the same structural-drift pattern the 2026-09-11 baseline note already predicted. Phase 7 (B6) confirmed as an intentional no-op: revisit trigger has not fired. Three commits pushed to close-all-open-2026-09-22: 07da38b4, e8ea887b, d832869a.
nextStep: Phase 4 of PLAN_CLOSE_ALL_OPEN_2026-09-22.md (D1 Phase 3: a brand-new CONCEPT usable via REST with no restart -- the flagship B28 capability) is next by the plan's own ordering, but its own text is explicit that Phase 4A (a research spike) must run FIRST and produce a written safety design before 4B-4D start, and that design needs owner approval before any runtime-DDL code is written (data-loss-class risk). Do not start writing Phase 4 code without that approval. If the user wants to keep closing items instead of doing the research spike, the cheaper alternatives the plan itself flags as independent are Phase 5 (QUAL-41, RuntimeHost coverage -- verification only, no owner decision needed) or Phase 6 (a FRESH exhaustive B28 residual sweep, now that REG-240/241/242/243 are all closed -- classification stays LIFTED,PARTIAL until that sweep actually runs clean, per this session's own B28.yml note warning against restating without one). Read PLAN_CLOSE_ALL_OPEN_2026-09-22.md's Phase 4 section before starting the spike -- it already names the three confirmed blockers (no runtime DDL code path, CRUD registration baked at generation time, generated-ui-manifest.json is a static file) and what each sub-phase needs to answer.
verified: Every gate run in this session was through the digest runner. Phase 1: :kernel:test :adapters:runtime-support:test --rerun-tasks BUILD SUCCESSFUL (6 new tests, skipped=0); RED-proven twice (reloadOrchestrationSubscribers stubbed to no-op -- exactly 3 fail; closeOrchestrationSubscriptionsLocked call removed -- 3 of 4 fail, a measured surprise vs. the plan's own prediction of 1, documented in the ledger); REG-240's identityTables also independently RED-proven (reverted to cache-on-first-call, exactly 2 of 3 tests fail). run-runtimehost-gate.ps1 and -Only aiKnowledge both green with jar mtime-confirmed rebuilt. Phase 2: check-model-provider-injection.py calibrated both directions via git stash (fires on exactly the 2 original injection sites, silent once restored); new DocumentRenderControllerReloadTest confirmed via fresh JUnit XML (1 test, skipped=0); run-runtimehost-gate.ps1 and -Only aiKnowledge (with new step [49/49] confirmed running, not skipped) both green. Phase 3: RED-proven (uiMetadataCatalogsRefreshed field commented out -- exactly 1 of 897 RuntimeHost tests fails); one transient failure (PluginIpcChildProcessWindowsResourceLimitTest, a Windows Job Object memory-ceiling test unrelated to any of this session's changes, with a literal paging-file-too-small JVM warning in the same log) confirmed transient by an immediate clean retry. check-done-item-guards.py: 0 blocking findings after every phase. All work pushed; git status clean except session-state files this handoff itself updates.
